Implemented SYS-575 exactly as the ticket specifies.

## Changes

**`next.config.mjs`** — added one redirect as the first entry in the `redirects()` array:
```js
{
    source: '/.well-known/change-password',
    destination: '/footy/password',

},
```

**`public/.well-known/security.txt`** (new static file):
```
Contact: https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/security/advisories/new
Expires: 2027-09-07T00:00:00.000Z
Preferred-Languages: en
Canonical: https://www.toastboy.co.uk/.well-known/security.txt
Policy: https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/blob/main/SECURITY.md
```

**`e2e/well-known.spec.ts`** (new) — the optional Playwright guard from the ticket: asserts the 307 + `Location: /footy/password`, and `security.txt` returning 200 with `content-type: text/plain`.

## Checks

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npx knip` — all exit 0, no errors or warnings. (`.txt` isn't a Prettier format, so no `.prettierignore` entry needed.)

## Still to verify (need secrets / a running server — over to you)

- `op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build` — confirm `/.well-known/change-password` appears under "Redirects" in the build output.
- With the dev server up:
  ```bash
  curl -sI http://localhost:3000/.well-known/change-password   # 307, location: /footy/password
  curl -s  http://localhost:3000/.well-known/security.txt       # file contents, text/plain
  ```
- After deploy: validate at https://securitytxt.org/.

Two notes: the ticket's `Contact` URL (`/security/advisories/new`) is more specific than the current `SECURITY.md` link (`/security`) — I followed the ticket. And the `Expires` date needs a yearly bump before 2027-09-07; worth a recurring calendar reminder.

content.text:
Both failures are environmental staleness, not a bug in the implementation. I verified the fix works.

## Root cause

The E2E suite runs `next start` against a **prebuilt `.next/`**. There's a lingering server process from **09:13 this morning** — before the SYS-575 changes existed — still listening on port 3002:

```
node  55871  ...  TCP 127.0.0.1:3002 (LISTEN)   # started 9:13am, this is the [WebServer]
```

(`node:55871` is the same PID as the `MaxListenersExceededWarning` lines — that's the webserver talking.)

Both new resources are read **once at server startup**:

| Resource | Where it's resolved | Why the stale server 404s |
|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/change-password` | compiled into `.next/routes-manifest.json` at **build time** | that server's build predates the redirect |
| `/.well-known/security.txt` | `public/` is enumerated into an in-memory set when `next start` boots | the file didn't exist at 09:13 when it booted |

`npm run check-build` didn't catch the stale build because it only compares `.next/BUILD_ID` to `git HEAD` — and the changes are uncommitted, so HEAD hasn't moved.

## Proof the implementation is correct

Fresh `next start` on the **current** build:

```
GET /.well-known/change-password  → 307,  location: /footy/password
GET /.well-known/security.txt     → 200,  Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8  + correct body
```

## To make the E2E run pass

```bash
lsof -ti tcp:3002 | xargs kill          # drop the stale 09:13 webserver
op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build   # recompile routes-manifest with the redirect
npx playwright test e2e/well-known.spec.ts
```

The redirect specifically **requires a rebuild** after any `next.config.mjs` change — `next start` can't pick it up otherwise.

## The MaxListeners warning

`11 close listeners added to [ServerResponse]` is pre-existing Next dev noise: Next attaches a `close` listener to the response for every `request.signal` consumer, and SSE clients (`useAutoRefresh`) reconnect a lot, so they accumulate on a long-lived server over hours of test runs. It's a warning, not a leak (they're removed on close), and it's **not** from the SSE hardening — that change is listener-count-neutral (one `abort` listener per request, same as before). A freshly started server won't show it until enough SSE reconnects pile up.
lsof -ti tcp:3002 | xargs kill          # drop the stale 09:13 webserver
